name: UK Developing Countries Trading Scheme (DCTS)
statusNote: In force since 19 June 2023. Rules-of-origin changes took effect on 1 January 2026.
summary: A UK scheme that cuts tariffs for eligible developing countries. Bangladesh is listed in the Comprehensive Preferences tier. India is among the countries covered by the scheme's rules-of-origin cumulation groups.
sectors: Range of goods. Rates are product-specific.
rules: Rules of origin apply. Goods must meet the scheme's origin rules and be processed for export to the UK in an eligible country.
links: Rules of origin changes now in effect (GOV.UK)

name: EU Generalised Scheme of Preferences, including Everything But Arms (EBA)
status: In force; new regulation applies from 1 January 2027
statusNote: The revised EU GSP Regulation applies from 1 January 2027. The European Commission says Bangladesh, scheduled to graduate from UN LDC status in 2026, will continue receiving EBA preferences for three further years, at least until the end of 2029. This is a transition in EU preferences; it does not change the UN graduation date.
summary: Bangladesh currently benefits from EBA as a least developed country. The EU transition period preserves EBA preferences for three years after LDC graduation, at least through the end of 2029. Product eligibility, origin rules and any safeguard measures still need to be checked for each shipment.
sectors: All products except arms and ammunition (under EBA).
rules: EU rules of origin apply, with product-specific rules. Check Access2Markets for your product.
links: Questions and answers on the new GSP (European Commission)

name: India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
statusNote: Signed on 24 July 2025 and in force since 15 July 2026.
summary: Reduces UK tariffs on Indian goods and covers services and other areas. Preferential treatment depends on the product meeting the agreement's rules of origin and following its administrative requirements.
sectors: Goods and services. Check the tariff schedule for your product.
rules: Rules of origin apply and must be met to claim preferences.
links: Ministry of Commerce and Industry, India: entry into force announcement

name: EU-India Free Trade Agreement
statusNote: Negotiations concluded in January 2026. The European Commission proposed signature and conclusion to the Council in September 2026. The agreement is not yet in force; the required EU and Indian approval steps remain.
summary: A concluded but not yet effective agreement. It does not change duties currently payable; check official sources for status and product-specific tariff schedules.
sectors: Goods, services and investment. See the Commission's summary.
rules: Rules of origin were agreed but only apply once the agreement is in force.

name: WTO Regional Trade Agreements database
statusNote: An official database of notified regional trade agreements.
summary: Use it to look up agreements that involve a country you are interested in.
